## TL;DR

The shell cross-fade and all added leave-state out-of-flow positioning are removed. The loader now swaps immediately between its shell and the route. Show-delay, minimum-visible time, reduced-motion behavior, the one-block Mission Control skeleton, Stories layout, named placeholder counts, and the related tests remain. The focused UI tests and `repoos check --changed main` passed.

## Work and rationale

The final owner decision moved the shell fade-out to follow-up #1078. I removed the shell-level Vue Transition wrapper so the loading shell unmounts as soon as its condition clears and the RouterView renders in normal flex flow. I removed the shell fade and absolute positioning CSS, and removed the temporary relative positioning on `.main` and route stacking rule that existed only to support that overlay.

The same scope defers leave animation and out-of-flow handling for individual PageSkeleton instances. I removed those leave styles and the test that required them, retaining the skeleton’s entry fade and reduced-motion suppression. Delay and minimum-visible timing remain in PageSkeleton’s deferred shell behavior.

The existing layout audit is unchanged:

| Page kind | Real layout | Skeleton shape |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mission Control | Full-width panel stack | One full-width block |
| Stories and row pages | Vertical lists | Representative rows |
| Work and Inputs | Multi-column boards | Columns using shared board constants |
| Agents, Checks, Dev, Deployments | Cards, table rows, target blocks, deployment blocks | Named counts for each shape |
| Settings | Grouped settings rows | Explicit grouped row count |

## Approaches tried

An earlier iteration overlaid the outgoing shell absolutely while the incoming route entered. That kept the old shell visible, but reviews found flex compression and then an inset mismatch with `.main` padding. The final decision removed this transition altogether, so those geometry fixes and their tests were removed instead of maintained.

## Challenges and blockers

The linked worktree had read-only source permissions at the start of this turn; restoring owner write permission allowed the scoped edit. The first remote validator attempt hung on ThinkPad and RepoOS retried on Bee. The retry passed the build and all 5,106 scoped tests, with one skipped; the rendered contrast audit and UI smoke also passed. The focused app-loading and page-height suites passed 23 tests. No new blocker remains.

## Key learnings

A visually smooth exit is not required when its layout complexity creates review churn and the owner has explicitly deferred it. Keeping the loading shell and route in a single normal-flow conditional gives a simpler, predictable swap. The minimum-time and show-delay behavior is independent of that transition and can remain without delaying the route after the shell hides.
